title: Hormuz LNG partial-recovery signal
net_new_delta: September LNG exits through Hormuz rose to the highest monthly level since the US-Iran war began, but remained far below pre-war normal; this adds a graded LNG-corridor recovery state distinct from crude transit evidence.
facts: Reuters reported S&P Global Energy counted 19 LNG cargoes through Hormuz in September: 13 Qatar and 6 UAE, versus 15 in June.
Reuters reported Kpler counted 21 September LNG exits, also versus 15 in June.
S&P said sustained late-September acceleration could bring October full-month transits to about 25% of pre-war levels.
source_claims: S&P Global Energy and Kpler independently indicate September was the highest monthly LNG transit count since the war began.
Analysts caution that dark transits, escalation risk, and winter sustainability remain unresolved.
model_inference: Treat Hormuz LNG operability as partially recovering but severely impaired; do not infer normalization or extrapolate LNG transit recovery to crude/product flows.
unknowns: Whether October sustains the late-September acceleration
Actual LNG volume versus cargo count
conflicts: Higher LNG transit counts coexist with projectile attacks on tankers and extensive AIS-dark transits, so physical operability and security risk remain simultaneously elevated.
affected_assumptions: Crude transit evidence can proxy LNG corridor recovery
next_decisive_check: Compare October LNG cargo counts and volumes with pre-war baseline, vessel AIS/dark-transit evidence, war-risk insurance and any new security incidents.

oracle.finding: Hormuz LNG transit evidence supports a partial-recovery state while remaining far below normal, requiring graded rather than binary corridor-operability assumptions.

supermesh_x.finding: Independent S&P and Kpler cargo counts converge directionally; route future confirmation through cargo counts plus volumes, AIS/dark-transit evidence and security/insurance data rather than extrapolating from crude movements.
